text:
maya: Heads-up — Polaris v0 model files uploaded and ready for serving-readiness checks. Weights + quantized builds are in s3://redwood-models/polaris/v0/. Draft model card and a short customer announcement are in a docs PR (link below). Targeting hosted launch EOD Wed if no blockers. Please review tokenizer quirks, config validation, and perf numbers.

aj: Which exact S3 keys and do we have checksums?

maya: Files: 
- s3://redwood-models/polaris/v0/polaris-v0.pt
- s3://redwood-models/polaris/v0/polaris-v0-4bit.bin
- s3://redwood-models/polaris/v0/metadata.json (includes tokenizer name + sha256 checksums)
Checksums (sha256): polaris-v0.pt = abc123f... (truncated), polaris-v0-4bit.bin = def456a...

simon: I'll kick off config validation + a small smoke serving test on p4d later today. Any recommended default serving config (seq len, batching, kv cache expectations)?

maya: Default config in infra/model-configs/polaris-v0.yaml in the repo. TL;DR: max_seq_len: 2048, max_batch: 8 for hosted; dedicate max_batch: 16 for Dedicated with 48GB GPUs. Expect KV cache ~3.2GB for 2k seq per replica. Also included a quantization profile in the same dir.

lia: You mentioned a tokenizer quirk — can you describe the behaviour and whether it will affect our existing SDK/clients?

maya: Quirk: the training tokenizer sometimes collapses consecutive leading spaces. Example:
```
input: "  Hello world"
expected tokens: ["▁", "Hello", "world"]
actual tokens: ["Hello", "world"]
```
This mostly affects prompts that rely on explicit leading whitespace (e.g., some code formats or aligned columns). For normal chat prompts it's fine. Mitigation: SDK shim option `normalize_whitespace=true` that inserts a placeholder leading token when leading spaces detected. I'll add a short note in the model card and a small wrapper in the python SDK.

aj: I'll add normalize_whitespace flag to the SDK shim in PR #2345 and run quick regression tests.

deploy-bot: CI started for infra/model-configs#polar-is-readiness (job: config-validate, smoke-serving-test) :rocket:

simon: Quick smoke results: generation looks good. Perf: ~120ms/token @ batch=1 on p4d. At batch=8 we see ~35ms/token. Note: small regression on numeric reasoning tests — accuracy down ~4% vs baseline on our math suite. I logged failing cases to the eval run.

maya: Good catch. Add that to the Known Limitations section in the model card: "reduced arithmetic/numeric reasoning compared to baseline; avoid for heavy numeric workloads." Also add the tokenizer whitespace note.

lia: For customer-facing naming, proposal: internal id `polaris-v0`, external label `Polaris` or `Polaris Code`. Thoughts?

maya: Preference: keep external simple: "Polaris" and subtitle in docs: "Polaris — Code & Chat optimized". In the API we'll expose model_id `polaris-v0` so nothing breaks.

aj: Docs PR looks fine to me. I'll merge once CI is green and once maya approves the model card.

maya: :thumbsup: I'll review the model card and the announcement blurb by noon. Draft announcement (customer-facing blurb):
"Polaris: a fast, 2k-context model optimized for conversational and code generation tasks. Best for chat assistants and code authoring workflows. Known quirks: minor arithmetic regressions on heavy numeric tasks; tokenizer may collapse leading spaces in rare cases — use our SDK `normalize_whitespace` option to preserve leading-formatting. Available now in hosted mode (model_id: polaris-v0)."

simon: I'll attach the smoke test logs and the failing eval examples to the PR.

aj: Action items:
- aj: add SDK shim (PR #2345)
- simon: upload smoke test logs + eval failures
- maya: update model card + approve docs PR
- lia: finalize external naming and short blurb for product marketing

maya: Thanks all — ping me if anything blocks CI.

deploy-bot: infra/config-validate passed. smoke-serving-test running...

(End of thread)
